title: contains_eager() .propagate_to_loaders doesn't work for a composite load option

labels.name: loader options
labels.description: ORM options like joinedload(), load_only(), these are complicated and have a lot of issues

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

body:
**Describe your question**

I have some code where I query for all instances of a model with some grandchildren `joinedload`. When I run an `update` on that model it then throws an error.

```py
DBBase = declarative_base()

class UserInventory(DBBase):
    user_inventory_id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    inventory_id = Column(
        Integer, ForeignKey('inventory.inventory_id'),
        nullable=False
    )
    is_checked = Column(Boolean, default=False)
    inventory = relationship('Inventory', back_populates='user_sets')

class UserPart(DBBase):
    user_part_id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_inventory_id = Column(
        Integer,
        ForeignKey('user_inventory.user_inventory_id'),
        nullable=False
    )
    inventory_part_id = Column(
        Integer,
        ForeignKey('inventory_part.id'),
        nullable=False
    )
    num_missing = Column(Integer, default=0, server_default='0')
    part = relationship('InventoryPart')
    user_set = relationship('UserInventory', back_populates='missing')
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(user_inventory_id, inventory_part_id, name='mp_uniq'),
    )

class InventoryPart(DBBase):
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    inventory_id = Column(
        Integer, ForeignKey('inventory.inventory_id', ondelete='CASCADE'),
        nullable=False
    )
    part_id = Column(
        TEXT, ForeignKey('part.part_id'),
        nullable=False
    )
    color_id = Column(
        Integer, ForeignKey('color.color_id')
    )
    part = relationship('Part', overlaps='element, part_id')
    color = relationship('Color', overlaps='element, color_id')

UI_ID = 1

parts = session.query(UserPart).\
        join(InventoryPart).\
        filter(UserPart.user_inventory_id == UI_ID).\
        order_by(
            InventoryPart.is_spare,
            InventoryPart.color_id
        ).\
        options(
            contains_eager(UserPart.part).joinedload(InventoryPart.part),
            contains_eager(UserPart.part).joinedload(InventoryPart.color)
        ).all()

session.query(UserPart).filter(UserPart.user_inventory_id == UI_ID).\
                update({"num_missing": 0}, synchronize_session="fetch")
session.commit()
```

**Complete stack trace, if applicable**
It throws this error on `session.commit()`
```
/Users/<me>/.pyenv/versions/env1/lib/python3.8/site-packages/sqlalchemy/orm/strategies.py:2580: SAWarning: Multiple rows returned with uselist=False for eagerly-loaded attribute 'UserPart.part' 
  util.warn(
```

I tried removing the `synchronize_session` option and it changed nothing. If I run the update and *then* run my `parts`
query, then no issues. It obviously has something to do with the joins before the update I think? 

**Versions**
 - OS: Mac Catalina 10.15.2
 - Python: 3.8.2
 - SQLAlchemy: 1.4.11
 - Database: SQLite
 - DBAPI:
